# OpenCode Loop 0.6.10 — standalone native OpenCode 2 release

Released after exact-main CI and registry verification only. Source merge or a passing PR is **not** proof that npm publication completed.

## What's new
- **Independent Loop**: `npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.10` installs Loop only, and `--uninstall` unregisters Loop only. `--with-goals` and `--with-loop-goals` now return an error before changing config. The separate `@bybrawe/opencode-goal` package is not installed, updated or removed by Loop.
- **Native OpenCode Goal 2.2.x safety**: when a built-in `/goal` is active or paused, Loop uses the host's public, read-only `opencode.goal` RPC to defer autonomous Loop admission in that session. Unknown states fail closed. The previous ByBrawe Goal's on-disk guard remains for installed clients; old files do not reserve sessions after that package is confirmed absent. These checks mitigate overlap but do not constitute an atomic scheduling guarantee; use separate sessions for separate autonomous jobs.
- **Native read-only TUI sidebar**: status RPC, session switching, safe read-only status rendering. Thanks to **[@zhek](https://github.com/zhek)** for the original [#165](https://github.com/ByBrawe/opencode-loop/pull/165) contribution, integrated as [#190](https://github.com/ByBrawe/opencode-loop/pull/190).
- **Cleaner installation**: explicit `OPENCODE_CONFIG` override recognized on removal; JSONC user comments and unrelated plugins preserved; dropped unnecessary V1-SDK npm peer to prevent clean consumer resolver conflicts.

## Install or remove

```powershell
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.10
# Later, if desired:
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.10 --uninstall
```

Quit and reopen the OpenCode backend, then check `/loop-doctor` and `/loop-status` in the same project/workspace. If an explicit config is used, set `OPENCODE_CONFIG` or `OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR` accordingly when removing. Project history under `.opencode/opencode-loop` is preserved.

OpenCode 2.2.x has a built-in `/goal`; seeing it after uninstalling our third-party Goal is expected and does not mean the removed package is still present.

## Explicit limitations
- The Loop TUI sidebar has OpenTUI 0.5.14/0.7.0 render tests, but **remote/split-cache CLI auto-discovery** is still tracked upstream and in [#191](https://github.com/ByBrawe/opencode-loop/issues/191). Its absence must never stop the scheduler.
- Windows Desktop/Web GUI native slash-command discovery is **not proven** ([#169](https://github.com/ByBrawe/opencode-loop/issues/169)); the OpenTUI renderer is not the Desktop GUI.
- Multi-agent Goal/Loop scheduling is not atomic across independent plugins; avoid running both autonomous engines in the same session.
- Historical `v0.6.6` tag permission issue [#168](https://github.com/ByBrawe/opencode-loop/issues/168) is separate release bookkeeping and is not silently claimed fixed.
- Publication must pass strict clean npm consumer, package manifest, source-to-Bun-bundle parity, Windows/Linux/macOS host test and immutable npm registry identity gates.

# OpenCode Loop 0.6.9

## Native OpenCode 2 checklist completion guard (#174)

Loop now supports **opt-in host-verified checklist completion** for user-owned project Markdown files. This addresses the real user report in which all tasks in TASK.md were checked but an intentionally unlimited idle Loop kept running.

Example:

~~~text
/loop --progress-file TASK.md --until-checklist-complete --verify "npm test" finish remaining project work
~~~

The **--until-checklist-complete** flag is explicit: an ordinary **--progress-file** is context only and does **not** change the existing unlimited Loop continuation contract. At a safe scheduling boundary, the host reads the Markdown file and requires at least one task checkbox with **zero unchecked tasks**. It ignores fenced code/quoted/commented examples. Missing, unsafe, symlinked, outside-project, control-plane, empty/unreadable or oversized paths never authorize completion; Loop pauses visibly instead.

When **--verify** is present, completion requires the host's successful verification recorded for the **exact SHA-256 content** of the checklist file. If TASK.md changes after a successful verification, the old result cannot stop the updated task. This is a file-content consistency check, **not** independent semantic evidence that untested work was correct.

Both native V2 and explicit V1 compatibility runtimes use the guard. Deterministic parser/filesystem, safe idle prompt suppression, stale-verification, bundle parity and Loop+Goal coexistence tests are required release gates.

## Native stop controls and OpenCode 2 diagnostics

Invoke /loop-stop or /loop-clear as a **real user slash command**. An AI assistant merely printing /loop-clear does not invoke the host command. /loop-status shows the opt-in checklist state and actionable stop information for active jobs.

Read-only Windows Desktop diagnostics can compare the CLI backend and an explicit localhost Desktop backend across two workspace directories, but the original Desktop GUI command discovery issue [#169](https://github.com/ByBrawe/opencode-loop/issues/169) is **not** claimed fixed until field replay.

## Package installation and verification

~~~text
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.9
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-goal@1.3.49
~~~

Install packages separately; Loop never silently installs or updates dedicated Goal. Fully quit and restart OpenCode, verify /loop-doctor, /loop-status, /goal status, and a short bounded Loop run in the intended project directory. Only rely on the new flag after 0.6.9 is present in the npm registry and the full published-package consumer workflow has succeeded. If publication fails, do not treat the GitHub source commit as an npm release.

This release does **not** claim all Windows Desktop/WSL/ARM64 GUI scenarios are solved.

# OpenCode Loop 0.6.8

## exFAT/FAT project volume lock compatibility (#172)

When `fs.link()` cannot claim a Loop session lock because hard links are unsupported (`EISDIR` on the reported Windows exFAT case, or `ENOTSUP`/`EOPNOTSUPP`/`ENOSYS`/`EPERM`/`EACCES`), Loop attempts an atomic `wx` exclusive-file claim instead.

The fallback also applies to dead-owner cleanup elections. A different live owner always wins; malformed lock owner metadata remains fail-closed, and unexpected I/O errors are not ignored. Short empty-owner publication windows get bounded retries instead of false corruption reports.

Tests exercise synthetic exFAT-style errors in independent Node processes, concurrent updates, abandoned locks and broken metadata. Windows/Linux, real OpenCode 2 and production artifact validation remain release gates. **Physical Windows exFAT and Desktop GUI behavior require separate field verification.**

## Independent installation

```powershell
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.8
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-goal@1.3.49
```

Fully exit and restart OpenCode. From the affected exFAT project, verify `/loop-status`, `/loop-doctor`, a short `/loop` job, and `/goal status`. Dedicated Goal remains a separately installed plugin; `/loop-goal*` compatibility commands are opt-in.

# OpenCode Loop 0.6.7

OpenCode 2 native reliability and package parity patch, tested alongside **separately installed** OpenCode Goal 1.3.48.

## Changes

- Protect per-session Loop state across multiple OpenCode processes with file locks, fail-closed corrupt-file reads, crash/dead-owner lock recovery and atomic writes on Windows/Linux.
- Restore manual native compaction with the public OpenCode 2 `session.compact` capability, requiring its exact manual compaction input ID, completion and terminal. Reject unsupported hosts without corrupting scheduled work.
- Provide read-only Windows Desktop native `/loop` and `/goal` command-catalog diagnostics and explicit project-directory comparisons. This is **not** a claim that Windows Desktop GUI autocomplete is fixed upstream.
- Bound Loop+Goal Windows cold-server startup probes and separate unresponsive host bootstrap from real Loop/Goal ownership conflicts.
- Align native `/loop-help` with the current V2 compaction contract.

## Install independently

```powershell
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.7
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-goal@1.3.48
```

A normal Loop install touches Loop only; it never installs or updates the dedicated Goal package. Legacy `/loop-goal*` commands stay opt-in, and existing state is preserved.

## Verification

When npm confirms publication, fully restart OpenCode and run `/loop-help`, `/loop-doctor`, `/goal status` in terminal TUI. For Windows Desktop use the [read-only diagnostic](../docs/OPENCODE2-DESKTOP-WINDOWS.md) without adding Markdown slash-command bridges.

Required release gates: immutable Goal source, Windows/Ubuntu package regressions, exact-main CI, installed-pair real host and clean npm consumer checks. GitHub tag and release creation require separate repository authorization, which may fail independently of verified npm publication.

# OpenCode Loop 0.6.5

OpenCode 2.0.22 SDK-contract patch, paired with OpenCode Goal 1.3.44.

## OpenCode 2.0.22 runtime contract

Loop's production `@opencode/plugin` dependency is pinned to exact 2.0.22. The
lockfile carries the matching `@opencode/{ai,client,protocol,schema,util}` runtime
closure so clean installs and release builds use the same native contract.

The moving real-host gate loads Loop main and the Goal companion together on
OpenCode 2.0.22. The exact OpenCode 2.0.18 native pair remains in CI as a
backwards-compatibility contract rather than being replaced by the current-host
check.

## Validation

The release candidate is gated by:

- Ubuntu and Windows native bundle/regression/package-smoke jobs;
- the real OpenCode 2 adapter;
- exact OpenCode 2.0.18 Loop+Goal coexistence;
- latest OpenCode 2.0.22 Loop+Goal coexistence;
- OpenCode 1 peer-compatibility tests.

## Upgrade

```sh
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-goal@1.3.44
npx -y @bybrawe/opencode-loop@0.6.5 --loop-only --without-loop-goals
```

Then fully restart OpenCode and verify:

```text
/goal status
/loop-help
/loop-doctor
```

Loop state, installer canonicalization, V1 compatibility, and the host-owned
automatic compaction boundary are unchanged by this SDK patch.
